findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates queries again downstream, so ad hoc filters can be added more than once
findings.body:
`runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on each target. It then passes each sub-request to `runSplitQuery`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `request.filters` (querySplitting.ts:299). After that, `datasource.runQuery`, which goes through the backend `query` path, normally applies template variables a third time.

The old code used `interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets, scopedVars)` and did not pass `filters`. The new call does pass `request.filters`. Loki's `applyTemplateVariables` appends ad hoc filters to the expression, so running it repeatedly can add the same label matchers or label filters more than once (e.g. `| key="v"` repeated) unless every path is idempotent.

Re-interpolation also means a substituted variable value that itself contains `$name` or `${...}` text gets interpolated a second time.

The test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times (1 + 4 sub-requests), which bakes in this double interpolation instead of catching it.

Fix: interpolate once at the entry point, for example by letting `runSplitQuery` skip interpolation when called from the shard path or via an option, and drop `filters` from the pre-interpolation if the backend path already applies them.

findings.title: Front-loaded interpolation passes ad hoc filters that the backend query path likely applies again
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now runs `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target before splitting. The resulting sub-requests keep `filters` (`{ ...request, targets }`) and are sent through `datasource.runQuery`. That backend `query` path normally calls `applyTemplateVariables` per target again with the request's filters.

As a result, ad hoc filters and variable substitution run twice on the already-interpolated expressions. Depending on how ad hoc filters are merged, this can duplicate filters in the final LogQL. It also re-processes values that were already substituted.

Only `$__auto`/`$step` need to be resolved before splitting. Consider interpolating without `filters`, or stripping `filters`/`scopedVars` from the sub-requests, so the backend path does not apply them again.
